name: ab_perfect_mul_abundant
statement: (n k : ℕ) (hn : Nat.Perfect n) (hk : 1 < k) : Nat.Abundant (k * n)
closed: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (hn : Nat.Perfect n) (hk : 1 < k), Nat.Abundant (k * n)
informal: Corrected task: a proper multiple (k > 1) of a perfect number is abundant.
original: If a student realised that the statement is false for k = 1, they were then prompted to provide a proof for k > 1.

attempts.note: released untouched: agent assigned to r3_ tasks only. Idea: image of properDivisors n under (k*·) plus {1} is a subset of properDivisors (k*n), sum = k*n+1.
